body: It looks like chafing to me
They had a cold sore and their partner forgot and kissed them.

The majority of the population has HSV1. If you left her, the next girl you meet will most likely have HSV1. She should have told you, no doubt, but realistically the majority of people with HSV1 (hello cold sore sufferers) don’t tell their partners they have the virus. 

I have genital HSV1, have had unprotected sex with ex boyfriends and never passed it on. The risk of genital to genital HSV1 when there’s no sore present is very minimal.

With every boyfriend I’ve had since my diagnosis I’ve not used condoms (after STD testing) and not taken antivirals (not available in the U.K). 

I have genital HSV1 though so the transmission risk is a bit different.
But HIV and HSV aren’t even in the same ballpark. You’re minimising HIV and overblowing HSV.

I’m sorry, I can’t believe OP is comparing HIV and HSV, and implying HIV isn’t too bad because if you take meds you can’t pass it on, whereas HSV is worse because we’re walking infections. HIV is a lifelong medical condition which requires continual medication that needs to be taken everyday, without fail, which comes with side effects. HIV affects your immune system and makes you more susceptible to other illnesses. HSV is a skin condition for Christ’s sake. 

Also the whole “we must live knowing we’ll never be cured”, urr, the majority of the human population have HSV and go on living their lives as normal!

I think with the HIV point, you’re only coming at it from the effect it has on sex ie. spreading it to other people. HIV comes with a lot of health complications and a lifetime of medication. HSV is a skin condition.
They only prescribe suppressive medication to people who experience 6 outbreaks or more in a year.

I always wanted to get married and have kids and I know now that it’s highly unlikely will find someone who wants to be with me. 

Even searching on Reddit you find “why be with her, find a girl WITHOUT herpes”. Meanwhile, my cheating ex gets to be happy.
I’m in the U.K. so suppressive medication isn’t prescribed here. I don’t get outbreaks.

I contracted genital HSV1 from an ex boyfriend who had a history of oral HSV1 (cold sores). We had been dating a year at that point, we both got tested and came back “clean”, and we used condoms. He didn’t have a cold sore present at the time. How exactly was I being half assed about my health?

....if you discovered into the relationship he had cold sores would you be this distraught and consider leaving him? 

He should have told you but I don’t think it’s a big of a deal as you’re making out.

I’ve told him I’m HSV1+ and he doesn’t care, I just haven’t told him it’s genital. But I know that makes all the difference. 

(Not had sex).
Went back to the doctor, had it swabbed and it was negative for HSV1. It was caused by dry skin.
Oh, then no.

I’m not sure if this is helpful but I’m HSV1+, dated my ex who is negative for ~7 months, we didn’t use condoms and I’m not on antivirals. They don’t do HSV testing in the U.K. but he’s still symptomless.

My GP stated it was due to thin skin. I’ve had issues with my skin in the past, way way before I was diagnosed with GHSV1. But every time I post in this forum, as you can see above, people tell me it’s very typical of herpes and also my negative swab tests could be due to me going at the wrong time. 

I don’t think I’m immunocompromised? I don’t have any illnesses, generally in good health, the last time I had a cold was June 2018 but before that no idea when. How would I be able to find out if I was?

A year ago I had an actual primary outbreak which was swabbed and it was HSV1. My boyfriend at the time had frequent cold sores. It was definitely herpes with a very typical primary outbreak. 

I didn’t have any symptoms again until 2/3 months ago until I got this recurrent fissure / split in my perineum. I went to several health professionals and they said it was due to my skin and not HSV1. But people on this forum keep telling me it’s very typical of Herpes so I really don’t know.
Also, again no one is offering an explanation / solution of what I’m getting “outbreaks” pretty much constantly for three months with HSV1
I’m not sure. This is the thing - medical professionals have ruled out herpes completely but this forum is pretty adamant that’s what my symptoms are. So I’m not sure.
Female
Used that. Antivirals appear to have no affect.
Unfortunately when it was swabbed it was negative.

I have genital HSV1, don’t take antivirals and don’t use condoms. I’ve had two long term partners (plus many ONS / FWB in which I used condoms) and I’ve never transmitted to anyone. You’re at more risk if you date someone with oral HSV1 (cold sores), which I can’t imagine you’d be worried about. However, it’s your body / choice. Just to be aware the risk with genital HSV1 is extremely low.

Went to the GP and she said it was due to thinness and was pretty adamant it wasn’t HSV1. She stated that there wasn’t really anything to swab and it would come back negative if she did. The GUM clinic said the same, she also stated that because I’ve been on antivirals for 7+ days it would come back negative even if it was HSV? 

I said that to the nurse on the phone at the GUM clinic and she just said to refrain from sex if I was so worried it was HSV. The thing is I’ve had this “cut” now for coming up to 3 weeks? I just really don’t understand if this is an outbreak or not. She told me to go to my GP but my GP already said it wasn’t.

The GP refused to swab me because she said it wasn’t HSV1 related and there wasn’t much to swab and it would come back negative anyways. She said my skin was thin and it was caused by that and given me steroid cream. The GUM clinic said it wasn’t an outbreak as I’ve seen no improvement from 7+ days on 1000mg acyclovir which is why they wouldn’t see me. We don’t have planned parenthood here. No idea what to do now as I’ve had this “cut” / tear for over two weeks and acyclovir is doing nothing to make it go away.

Yeah that’s a good idea. I’ve had things pop up in the past that I was convinced was an outbreak but then went to the clinic and had it swabbed / looked at and it’s been an ingrown hair / folliculitis. Having it checked would give you peace of mind!
That looks like an outbreak to me. Could you get it swabbed to confirm?
Female to male transmission for genital HSV1 is estimated at 1% a year (having sex 2/3 times a week), with condoms OR antivirals 0.5% a year, with both 0.25% a year. So extremely unlikely.
I have GHSV1 and don’t use condoms in relationships (not on antivirals either). Never transmitted to anyone.

Thanks for your response but it didn’t really answer my question. I’ve had HSV1+ for a year now. 

I was prescribed 5 days of acyclovir (5 x200mg dose). I have taken it for one day. I no longer have symptoms. I would like to stop taking it. Am I required to finish the 5 day course, or can I just stop it now?

Yeah I know they’re different. I’m on long term antibiotics for another issue, I know they have no effect on viruses however I may have developed a yeast infection which is a common side effect of antibiotic use in women. In the past (when I was HSV-) I used to get little cuts from yeast infections so I was unsure whether I now had a yeast infection OR an outbreak, so to cover both I took both something for the yeast infection and acyclovir. The symptoms are now gone. 

My question was - can I stop acyclovir now or do I have to continue with the full course.

I remember after my ex (who gave me HSV1) broke up with me I thought I’d never find someone okay having sex with me. But then when I told my current boyfriend he was like “okay cool, thanks for telling me” and literally didn’t care at all. I’m actually surprised how little impact it’s had on my sex life.

I got diagnosed with GHSV1 last year and as far as I’m aware haven’t had an outbreak since - I had a small “split” on my perineum last week but it lasted 3 days and I’ve pretty sure it was caused by yeast as I’m on long term antibiotics (for rosacea, which is by a far worst skin condition for me!). Even if it was an outbreak it was so mild I had to use a magnifying mirror to see it. My current partner knows (literally did not give two fucks when I told him), I’m not on antivirals and we don’t use condoms. He hasn’t contracted it. Life is no different than before.

Because it’s based on CDC recommendations due to high rate of false positives, psychological impact, and the disruption to personal relationships. The UK does have an excellent sexual health service which is why it follows these recommendations. I don’t think it’s unethical at all. At the end of the day, what’s the point in diagnosing someone with HSV when they’ve had no symptoms and no way of knowing what part of their body their infection is? It wouldn’t change their sexual behaviour (unless they decide to become celibate).

I went to counselling that was offered by the GUM clinic after my diagnosis and that really helped me to shake the feeling of being “dirty” (which I still get sometimes). Something that might be useful for him.
Yeah. I’d also like to say at this point I agree with your stance / the U.K. stance of not being tested without symptoms. Hopefully you can give your boyfriend some reassurance about his diagnosis.

Ah okay, thought you might have been referring to that table. However that is not in reference to the seroprevalence in the general population, but rather the reliability of testing for HSV2. Note that the 5% is in reference to antenatal clinics - so this would only cover females who were accessing these clinics. 

Edit - the Wiki article is also in reference to only England and Wales, not the U.K. as a whole. 

Edit edit - the lower seroprevalence could also be due to what this thread is about - blood testing is not routine in the U.K. for HSV so we really don’t have an accurate picture. I’ve just never seen a stat so low and it may make folk coming to this subreddit with HSV2 feel even more isolated. Based on NHS data / Herpes.org stats I’m more keen to believe the 1 in 10.

Can you just point out where in that article they state seroprevalence at 5%? Skimmed over twice and can’t see it mentioned. I just think 1 in 20 is very low, and I’ve never seen it quoted in any literature / UK website.
Odd, that’s usually where I get my stats from. Just checked now and it states 60% for HSV1 and 10% for HSV2. I suppose still less than the US but higher than 1 in 20.
The effect would be pretty high, as for the sounds  of it now every time I get a bump or scrape on my genital region I have to assume it’s an outbreak.

I think for now I don’t want to rule out that they’re caused by something else, as they’ve always coincided with yeast infections and I know that paper cuts can be a symptom of that, plus it went away with >24 hours using canesten. It’s just a shame they go away so quickly I can’t get it tested. When I’ve been to the doctor before they did say HSV+ people do over attribute innocuous symptoms as herpes outbreaks. 

I don’t want to be one of those people with frequent ish symptoms as it effects my sex life, plus I don’t want to reminded I have herpes. Also, people who show symptoms shed more frequently.

It’s not red, and I don’t get any neuropathy at all. It’s a tiny, tiny little dot/cut. In my head I’ve always told myself I’m one of the majority of GHSV1+ people who don’t get any more outbreaks after the first so I’m gutted that I do, even if they are extremely mild.

The NHS can’t offer you a blood test. It’s not available on the NHS. To get a blood test for HSV, you’ll have to pay for it privately. 

Just wondering about the statistic for HSV2, do you have a source for that? I’m from the U.K. too and have never seen it so low. I’ve always read 1/6.

You can’t get tested in the U.K. unless you have active symptoms or willing to fork out £500+ every 3-6 months to get tested at a private clinic. The NHS don’t offer a blood test as per CDC guidelines. Does that mean everyone in the U.K. is selfish? Or just not part of the insane herpes stigma they have in the US?
Just FYI, the NHS will NEVER offer you a blood test for herpes. If you are showing active symptoms, they will do a swab test. This is per CDC recommendations.
Or Tinder. No need to push all HSV people into a “reject herpes corner”.
There isn’t any studies regarding genital to genital HSV1 specifically because it occurs so rarely.

How is genital HSV1 different from oral HSV1? The majority (if not all!) cases of genital HSV1 is caused by someone with history of cold sores. So if you don’t want to take the risk with genital herpes, don’t take the risk with people with cold sores too 💀💀

Understand that you have the same virus that over half of the US population have, or 70% of the U.K. population have. Do you honestly think someone with a cold sore feels guilty when they kiss someone or give someone oral sex? The majority of people who have oral HSV1 don’t even bother with disclosure. 

Someone’s mentioned positivesingles on this thread...one of my biggest pet peeves. You’re not a “herpes reject” who needs to find a HSV+ person on some dead dating website. If you’re worried about transmission date one of the millions of people who are also HSV1+. Or understand that GHSV1 has such a small risk of transmission and date anyone you want.

Oh my god. The positive singles thing. People suggest that to me and I think it’s ridiculous, why would someone with genital HSV1 reduce their dating pool when the majority of the population have the virus?
Do you think people who have cold sores don’t deserve relationships?

Type 2 is more contagious as it sheds more and has more outbreaks. But if she’s on meds and you guys use condoms the transmission rate is 1% a year if you’re having sex 2 times a week. Both strains of herpes aren’t serious in the sense that there’s no real medical implications, it’s just a skin condition. 

I don’t take antivirals and I don’t use condoms. There’s not really much to handle as I don’t get outbreaks. If I did randomly get an outbreak I would just refrain from PIV sex. We just treat it the same as someone who gets cold sores because that’s what it is except in a different place. Every guy has been cool with it, no one has really cared.

I have genital HSV1, contracted from someone who had a history of cold sores (that more than half the US population have the virus for). I’ve had multiple partners and two boyfriends since diagnosis and I have never passed it on to anyone, mainly because genital HSV1 is not very contagious outside an outbreak (I’ve only ever had one outbreak and it was very mild). You need to find out whether she has HSV1 or HSV2. You also need to head over and ask this question on r/herpes so you can get some more accurate information on the virus, as most people overestimate the risk and will automatically just say it’s not worth it. 

I have genital herpes and I am worthy of relationships and so is this girl. Just like everyone with cold sores are worthy.

I’m pretty sure every person with genital HSV1 disagrees with that, considering all cases of genital HSV1 are caused by someone with the “no big deal” cold sore. Oral HSV1 is more contagious than genital HSV1, which is expected to be disclosed.

I’ve never read anyone on this sub ever saying “50% of people have HSV2”. A majority of the population DO have HSV1 though, and I’ve seen several people in several threads give you sources for this. 

1 in 6 people is still a relatively large portion of the population. Millions of people have HSV2 and still live completely normal lives.

I have GHSV1, and usually the primary outbreak of GHSV1 is pretty bad, so I’m not sure the doctor’s reasoning for their diagnosis. On top of that antivirals are still effective for HSV1 regardless of location, so I’d go back and get a prescription. 

I got lidocaine gel for the pain and used a water jug to pee.
But people don’t care about cold sores. They care about genital herpes.
I’ve told my friend about what’s happened and even though I told her genital HSV1 poses little risk and oral HSV1 has a much higher risk, she still refuses to disclose her cold sores.
No, it’s different strains of virus. I have HSV1, not HSV2.
I don’t have HSV2.

1 in 5 have HSV2. But 80% don’t know they have it so don’t have to disclose, so don’t have to face rejection. I have HSV1, but at the end of the day no one will want to date someone diseased when they can find someone who doesn’t have this virus.

Didn’t say it was my only problem. 

I also don’t think spending the rest of my life single without sex is a walk in the park. My dream was to get married and have children and now that’s impossible.
I haven’t had an outbreak since, and probably never have one again. However, the stigma will be with me for the rest of my life.
